items.name: Conditional probability
items.when: When you know $B$ happened: only the cases with $B$ count, so divide by them.
items.cue: The definition of $P(A \mid B)$ as a fraction of two probabilities

items.name: The two directions differ
items.when: Whenever you read a conditional: the number under the line is the condition's group.
items.cue: Whether $P(A \mid B)$ and $P(B \mid A)$ are equal, with the spam example

items.name: Both at once
items.when: To get the share where both happen from a rate inside one group.
items.cue: $P(A \text{ and } B)$ written with a conditional probability

items.name: Law of total probability
items.when: To find the bottom of Bayes' rule: all the ways to see $B$, added.
items.cue: $P(B)$ split by the two cases $A$ and not $A$

items.name: Bayes' rule
items.when: To turn a test's accuracy into the chance the condition is there.
items.cue: Bayes' rule: $P(A \mid B)$ from $P(B \mid A)$, the prior and $P(B)$

items.name: Natural frequencies
items.when: When a table of 10,000 people is easier than probabilities.
items.cue: How to get $P(\text{sick} \mid \text{positive})$ by counting people

items.name: Odds
items.when: To change probability into the scale where updates multiply.
items.cue: The odds of $A$ in terms of $P(A)$

items.name: Odds to probability
items.when: At the end of an odds update, to get a probability again.
items.cue: Converting odds back to a probability

items.name: Likelihood ratio
items.when: To measure how strongly a piece of evidence points one way.
items.cue: The likelihood ratio of a positive test, from its two rates

items.name: Odds form of Bayes
items.when: To update by one multiplication, with no $P(B)$ to compute.
items.cue: The odds form of Bayes' rule, in words and symbols

sections.title: More than one piece of evidence

items.name: Update twice
items.when: When the two pieces are independent given each class (naive Bayes).
items.cue: Posterior odds after two pieces of evidence, with the ratios $L_1$ and $L_2$
